To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the percentage levels of T cells expressing activation markers (HLA- DR and CD25) are significantly increased in HIV-infected patients compared with healthy controls, and that levels of these activated T cell subsets are significantly associated with disease severity.
T cell activation, measured by HLA-DR expression and CD25 expression, is an early and consistent feature of HIV infection and is associated with progression of disease.

(1) HIV infection is associated with a marked increase in the percentage of activated T lymphocytes; (2) the increase is more pronounced in CD4+ than in CD8+ lymphocytes; (3) the increase in activated CD4+ lymphocyte is a consistent and early feature of HIV infection; and (4) levels of activated T lymphocyte subsets may be used as surrogate markers for disease progression in patients with HIV infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of immune cell activation in HIV infection and AIDS.
the development of a new method for monitoring the progress of HIV infection.
the development of a novel assay for the detection of T cell activation in HIV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T cell activation marker HLA-DR is a good indicator of HIV-related disease progression and that CD25 may be of value in monitoring the progression of asymptomatic HIV infection.
the T cell activation marker CD3+HLADR+ is a marker of disease severity and progression in HIV infection, and is a better indicator of progression than CD4+ counts or beta 2-micoglobulin levels.
T cell activation and disease progression are closely related in HIV infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T cell activation, especially of CD4+ T cells, is associated with the severity of disease in HIV infection.
HIV disease progression is characterized by a progressive increase in the proportion of activated T cells.

T cell activation, as measured by HLA-DR expression, is a sensitive marker for disease severity and progression in HIV infection, but that it is not a reliable indicator for the risk of disease progression in asymptomatic HIV-infected individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T-cell activation is an early feature in the HIV infection, and monitoring of T-cell activation may be useful in assessing progression of disease.
HIV infection is characterized by a high level of immune activation.
the immune activation marker HLA-DR is a more sensitive and reliable measure of disease progression than the CD4 count.
